MassPay Partners with Bottomline to Add Paymode Virtual Card and Premium ACH to Its Platform
summary:
Bottomline, a global leader in business payments, today announced a partnership with MassPay, a payment orchestration and global financial platform, to embed Paymode’s virtual card and Premium ACH capabilities directly into the MassPay platform. This will allow MassPay customers to pay U.S. vendors through Paymode’s secure network alongside the payments they already manage through MassPay.
As payment fraud targeting businesses continues to rise, finance teams need vendor payment methods that protect both sides of the transaction. MassPay customers will gain access to Paymode's wide network of enrolled vendors and can use virtual card and Premium ACH as secure vendor payment options. Businesses can reduce fraud risk, keep better control over who gets paid and how, and manage it all on the platform they already use. For organizations still paying some vendors by check, it also offers a simple path to secure electronic payments.
"Security is at the center of every payment our customers make," said Ran Grushkowsky, Co-Founder and CEO of MassPay. "Adding Paymode's services gives our customers secure ways to pay vendors, backed by a trusted network, without adding another system to manage."
"Finance teams are under pressure to protect against fraud while doing more with fewer resources," said Gunita Bindra, Vice President, Partnerships and Business Development at Bottomline. "MassPay has built a strong platform for moving money across a wide range of payment scenarios. Together, we're making it easier for their customers to automate vendor payments securely and move away from paper checks."
The partnership expands Bottomline’s embedded payments ecosystem by extending access to Paymode through strategic partners that help businesses pay and get paid digitally.

title: Diebold Nixdorf Enables stc pay Bahrain to Bridge Digital and Physical Financial Services
summary:
Diebold Nixdorf, a global leader in transforming the way people bank and shop, today announced that stc pay Bahrain will expand customer access to its digital financial services into physical locations with DN Series® cash recyclers and DN Vynamic® Software. The agreement represents Diebold Nixdorf's first major engagement with a telecommunications-affiliated financial services provider in the Middle East, demonstrating how the company's solutions can support emerging financial-services models beyond traditional banking. The announcement was made at Fintech Forward 2026 in Bahrain.
For stc pay Bahrain, the country's innovative and accessible mobile wallet for digital financial transactions and a subsidiary of stc Bahrain, the combination of physical self-service and digital capabilities will provide consumers with greater choice in how, when and where they transact, while supporting the Central Bank of Bahrain's vision for a modern, innovative and cash-optimized society.
stc pay Bahrain will install the DN Series cash recyclers, some featuring Interactive Teller Machine (ITM) kits, across its locations. Rather than functioning as traditional ATMs, the devices will serve as physical gateways to stc pay Bahrain's digital ecosystem, enabling customers to move seamlessly between cash, cards, mobile wallets and digital services. Customers can perform a broad range of transactions, including wallet top-ups, eSIM issuance, domestic and international remittances, bill payments, gift card purchases, transportation card top-ups, charitable donations and cash collections for small- and medium-sized businesses.
DN Vynamic Software will connect these physical touchpoints with stc pay Bahrain's digital services and payment infrastructure. Vynamic Transaction Middleware, a cloud-native, API-driven platform, orchestrates transactions across channels and makes it easier to introduce new services as consumer needs evolve. Vynamic Terminal Driving supports capabilities such as contactless payments, mobile wallets and real-time account access.
The DN Series devices are powered by DN AllConnectSM Data Engine, which leverages artificial intelligence and machine learning to maximize fleet performance and availability, together with Vynamic View software for 24/7 fleet monitoring and management.
The local deployment and technical support are being executed in collaboration with Almoayed Group WLL, Diebold Nixdorf's licensed partner in Bahrain.
Metin Zavrak, CEO of stc pay Bahrain, said: "Expanding our network beyond the mobile app is a strategic step towards making our financial services more accessible to the wider community. By introducing physical kiosks, we are providing customers with greater choice and flexibility in how they access and use our services, while extending our reach across Bahrain. Our partnership with Diebold Nixdorf enables us to deliver a secure, reliable and convenient experience, further strengthening our commitment to advancing financial inclusion."
Habib Hanna, managing director – Middle East, at Diebold Nixdorf said: "Our work with stc pay Bahrain demonstrates how an innovative, digital-first fintech can use our self-service technology and software to establish a physical presence, reach more consumers and offer a broader range of transactions. DN Series is evolving beyond the traditional ATM into a highly connected transaction point that can bring digital financial services into the physical world."

Beyond Cloud-Native: The Rise of the Agentic Enterprise
summary:
The global technology stack is quietly shifting from cloud‑native to AI‑native, and ultimately agent‑native. For executive teams, this is less a matter of collecting new acronyms and more a question of how their organisations will work, decide and compete over the next decade. This evolution represents a fundamental shift in cloud infrastructure: from managing computing power at scale to managing and orchestrating intelligence at scale.
From plumbing to behaviour  
To put it simply, cloud‑native was about plumbing: elastic infrastructure, containers and microservices that made software cheaper to scale and easier to ship. AI‑native marks a different kind of change—applications designed with models at the centre, not as decorative features glued onto legacy stacks. 
In AI‑native products, models are not “features”; they are the decision engines that interpret messy data, personalise experiences and automate judgments, from credit decisions to supply-chain forecasts.  That is why AI‑native platforms increasingly resemble operating systems for intelligence: they integrate models, data, feedback loops and human oversight into a single fabric that learns continuously.
For most enterprises, this phase has already begun in pockets—pilots in customer support, risk, marketing, and internal productivity tools—long before anyone updated the strategy slides.
The agent-native inflection  
Agent‑native goes further still. In this new paradigm, Intelligent agents are emerging as a new class of machine user alongside engineers and applications. Traditional cloud interfaces designed for human clicks are being rewritten into standardized skills and command-line tools that agents can natively understand and execute. Autonomous agents combine language models, memory and tool use to plan and execute multi‑step workflows across enterprise systems, with humans in the loop for supervision and judgment. McKinsey’s work on “the agentic organization” describes this as a new operating paradigm in which humans and AI agents work side by side at near‑zero marginal cost, reshaping the foundations of business models, operating models and governance.
Gartner, meanwhile, expects AI agents to move from niche experiments to standard infrastructure within this decade. One forecast suggests that by 2026, 40% of enterprise applications will integrate task‑specific AI agents, up from less than 5% in 2025. Another projects that average agent counts per large company could expand from around 15 in 2025 to tens of thousands by 2028, creating what they describe as “armies of digital workers” as well as a new class of governance challenges.
Why this matters to C‑level leaders  
First, the nature of “digital transformation” is changing from “systems of record” to “systems of action”. Cloud-native modernised plumbing; AI‑native and agent-native modernise behaviour, determining who (or what) makes which decisions at what speed.
In practical terms, agentic AI compresses cycle times between sensing, deciding and acting across the business—from detecting fraud to launching micro-campaigns and rerouting inventory. Companies that implement these loops early are not merely more efficient; they become structurally faster organisations, able to adjust strategy through software rather than reorganisations.
Second, the workforce model is quietly evolving. Some firms now talk about “onboarding non-human employees”: agents with email addresses, system credentials and defined responsibilities, supervised by humans. This raises thorny questions about accountability, audit, risk and culture—but it also opens the door to scaling capabilities without linear headcount growth.
Third, the build‑versus‑buy calculus is shifting. As AI makes bespoke software and workflow automation dramatically cheaper to assemble, boards will revisit reliance on monolithic Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) for processes that can instead be expressed as intent and orchestrated by agents. CIOs and CFOs will find that the cost curve of “owning” key capabilities looks different when AI can generate, maintain and adapt large portions of the stack.
Competitive advantage, quietly earned  
None of the analysts suggest that simply deploying more agents will guarantee success; indeed, Gartner warns of high failure rates for generative‑AI initiatives and emphasises the need for strong security and oversight as agents gain autonomy. Enterprise-grade agent-native clouds must therefore provide robust runtime sandboxes, identity management, and task-level security controls to safely govern these autonomous entities. McKinsey’s guidance is similarly cautious: the real gains show up only where organisations redesign workflows end‑to‑end to be AI‑first, embed human‑in‑the‑loop governance, and invest in culture and skills so that humans can work effectively with agents as colleagues rather than tools.
The competitive advantage, then, lies less in any single model and more in organisational imagination and execution. Early adopters that “agentify” carefully chosen workflows, build an internal platform layer for agents, and reshape roles around hybrid teams are likely to move faster and learn more cheaply than peers that treat agents as isolated pilots.
A humble agenda for the C‑suite  
This trend invites less bravado and more careful architecture. The temptation will be to declare an “agentic transformation programme”, but the wiser path is to treat agent-native as an operating thesis and move in measured steps.
A practical agenda might include:
Design for governance first. Put human‑in‑the‑loop checkpoints, audit trails and enterprise-grade identity and access controls at the heart of any agent roll‑out, rather than as compliance afterthoughts.
Create an “agent platform” layer. Standardize how agents access data, tools and credentials, using secure orchestration frameworks rather than bespoke integrations scattered across departments.
Treat speed of implementation as a competitive variable. Evidence from early adopters suggests that the advantage lies less in any single model and more in how quickly organisations can wire agents into real processes and iterate.
None of this requires executives to become AI theorists. It does, however, require treating agents as organisational units—subject to the same discipline of strategy, risk, measurement and culture as human teams.

Mastercard and BVNK Launch Global Money Platform to Power a Multi-Money World
summary:
Mastercard and BVNK today announced the launch of Mastercard Global Money Platform, bringing together Mastercard’s global payments capabilities with BVNK’s stablecoin infrastructure through a single API. The launch marks the first major integration of Mastercard and BVNK capabilities since the acquisition of BVNK in August 2026.
Global Money Platform provides a full-stack, modular infrastructure layer for modern finance. Banks, fintechs and enterprises can now embed multi-currency accounts, including fiat and stablecoins, real-time conversion, stablecoin-linked cards and local bank payouts through Mastercard Move into their own products and under their own brand. They can also use the platform to manage their own treasury, payments and settlement activity directly.
Customers can start with the capabilities they need and add more as they become available, reducing the need to integrate separate providers for each part of the money journey.
Payments leader Nuvei and modern card issuing platform Marqeta will be among the first to integrate Global Money Platform, alongside Ontop, Beem and Almond FinTech. The platform will enable customers to move more seamlessly between traditional currencies and stablecoins while expanding choice in how they accept, manage and move money across markets.
Consider a manufacturing business receiving multiple currencies and paying out global suppliers. Managing those flows today means juggling separate accounts, vendors and pre-funded balances across markets — tying up working capital and slowing down operations. Mastercard Global Money Platform simplifies that experience, giving businesses a single place to manage liquidity, move between fiat currencies and stablecoins, and handle receivables and payouts.
One platform, multiple forms of money
At the center of Global Money Platform is the global money account: a multi-currency account where fiat and stablecoins can sit side by side, with conversion between the two through a single API. The platform gives users flexibility in how they manage and move funds across stablecoins and fiat currencies through a single integration, alongside configurable rewards and other account features. Fintechs and technology platforms can embed these accounts into their platforms to give customers one place to hold, convert and pay out earnings.
The platform also integrates Mastercard Move, Mastercard’s portfolio of global money movement capabilities reaching more than 17 billion endpoints, enabling users to leverage stablecoin balances to make local currency payments directly into recipients’ local bank account, with coverage expected to expand to more than 40 currencies across 200-plus countries and territories in 2027.
Global Money Platform customers will be able to spend their stablecoin balances across Mastercard’s global acceptance network of hundreds of millions of merchant locations, with card issuing available across 130-plus countries.
Preparing for what’s next
Global Money Platform is a full-stack, modular toolkit spanning send, receive, convert, store, spend and earn, designed for a multi-money future, where new forms of money, networks and payment models continue to emerge. This includes future support for agentic commerce and additional regulated forms of money including tokenized deposits.

Wells Fargo Deepens AI and Data Leadership for Consumer Banking and Lending
summary:
Wells Fargo & Company today announced that Cayetano Gea-Carrasco is joining the company as head of AI and Data for Consumer Banking and Lending. He will report to Saul Van Beurden, head of Enterprise AI and co-CEO of Consumer Banking and Lending and will be based in San Francisco.
Gea-Carrasco will oversee the full lifecycle of AI use cases, simplify the data environment, and accelerate responsible delivery of AI for Consumer Banking and Lending. He also will partner with the Enterprise AI team to scale solutions across the company.
“Customers do not think about channels. They expect us to know them, make banking easier, and be there when they need us,” said Van Beurden. “Cayetano understands how strong data and disciplined execution turn AI into better customer experiences. His track record will help us move faster while keeping safety and sound risk management front and center.”
Gea-Carrasco joins Wells Fargo from BBVA, where he led enterprise AI transformation and its global data and analytics organization. He previously spent 15 years at Moody’s in senior roles spanning software data and analytics. He holds an MBA from the MIT Sloan School of Management and graduate degrees in financial mathematics and telecommunications engineering.
“Wells Fargo’s scale and depth of customer relationships create a powerful opportunity to put AI to work,” Gea-Carrasco said. “I’m joining to make everyday banking simpler for our customers and deliver measurable business outcomes, with the controls and accountability our customers expect.”

SWIVEL® Introduces PayPrompt® Pro
summary:
SWIVEL®, a subsidiary of SWBC and leading fintech company specializing in integrated solutions, announced the launch of PayPrompt® Pro, an enhanced digital payments communications solution designed to help financial institutions turn payment reminders into borrower action and accelerate reconciliation.
A key component of SWIVEL’s broader digital payments communications strategy, PayPrompt Pro enables lenders to deliver secure, personalized payment reminders directly within the channels borrowers already use and trust. Embedded within existing financial institution platforms, the solution combines SMS payment reminders, secure Reply-to-Pay functionality, deep-link payment experiences, and future-ready digital engagement capabilities to create a convenient, user-friendly payment journey.
Today’s borrowers increasingly expect seamless digital convenience, but growing concerns around payment fraud, spoofed messages, and phishing attempts have made trust just as important as speed. The solution addresses both needs by helping financial institutions deliver trusted payment experiences that reduce friction while reinforcing borrower confidence.
“Financial institutions have spent years making payments faster and more convenient, but increasingly, the challenge is making those interactions feel just as secure and trustworthy,” said Amanda Licona-Crocker, President of SWIVEL. “Borrowers want an easy way to stay on top of payments while knowing they are interacting with their financial institution in a familiar and trusted environment. PayPrompt Pro brings those experiences together.”
PayPrompt Pro includes several capabilities designed specifically for financial institution payment workflows:
Reply-to-Pay via SMS enables borrowers to respond instantly and directly to payment reminders with a simple “Y” to initiate payment, reducing friction while addressing concerns around clicking unknown links.
Automated Payment Reminders help lenders proactively engage borrowers before payments become delinquent.
Deep-Link Payments create streamlined, one-tap payment journeys that take borrowers directly to payment actions, with in-thread payment experiences designed to simplify the path from reminder to payment.
Native Platform Integration embeds communications directly into existing financial institution platforms, creating a seamless borrower experience.
White-Labeled Capabilities ensure the financial institution’s branding throughout the borrower journey, reinforcing trust and recognition.
Immediate Payment Confirmation gives borrowers the peace of mind that their payments have been successfully received and recorded.
Unlike broad communications platforms that treat payment prompting as just one of many features, PayPrompt Pro is purpose-built to support financial institution payment and lending strategies.
PayPrompt Pro is available now as a standalone SWIVEL solution for financial institutions seeking to modernize their borrower communications and payment engagement strategies.

The platform integrates SMS payment reminders, Reply-to-Pay functionality, and deep-link payment experiences to help lenders accelerate reconciliation and turn payment reminders into borrower action while ensuring security, trust, and native platform integration.
